absent: Numeric values and full enumeration of big-block and sub-block memory-block states
Address translation between block ids and physical addresses and block-size discovery
Workqueue handler behavior and unplug request path beyond requeue
Locking for per-block state get and set outside store growth
Hibernation veto rationale beyond unplug-on-restart statement

findings.text: Device tracks two block managers. Big-block manager holds first and next block ids, per-block state array, per-state counters, and block size. Sub-block manager holds first and next memory-block ids, per-block state bytes, per-state counters, subblocks-per-block and subblock size, plus a flat plugged bitmap over all subblocks. Device also carries address plus region size, offline accounting and threshold, hotplug mutex, removal lock with removing and hotplug-active flags, work item, and notifier blocks.

Per-block state is stored at identifier minus first identifier, and a companion counter per state records population. Updating one block decrements the old-state counter and increments the new-state counter; counters are asserted never to underflow. Forward and reverse scans over the identifier interval stop early when the sought-state counter reaches zero and test each entry for that state.

Subblock plugged state is one bit in a dense bitmap. Bit position is linear in memory-block offset times subblocks per block plus subblock index. Set and clear operate on a run; single-bit plugged test reads one bit while multi-bit plugged and unplugged tests scan for absence of the opposite value across the run; first-unplugged search reports offset within the block.

State stores grow by one logical entry using page-rounded allocation. If the page count is unchanged the existing store is kept; otherwise a fresh zeroed store is allocated outside locks, old contents copied under the hotplug mutex, and the device pointer swapped. The bitmap variant frees the old store only after unlocking.

Range membership is judged against device base and region length: overlap when intervals intersect, containment when the candidate lies wholly inside. NUMA translation defaults to no-node and only maps the supplied proximity id when the corresponding ACPI feature is present.

Offline accounting bounds growth. A size larger than the threshold is rejected; otherwise addition is allowed only while current offline total plus size stays within threshold. Successful memory addition pre-accounts the size and rolls back on failure; successful plain removal, and successful offline-plus-removal, subtract it. Removal paths requeue device work on success.

Adding memory lazily creates a persistent resource name once and registers managed memory with merge-resource and node-from-group semantics. Sub-block adds use host memory-block granularity at the block address; big-block adds use configured big-block size at the big-block address. Removal mirrors the same address derivation. Offline-plus-removal normalizes failures to out-of-memory or busy.

Sub-block memory-block online state distinguishes offline, offline-partial, kernel, movable, and partial online variants plus unused. Going-online is accepted only from offline-like states and otherwise denied. Offline transitions move online variants to the matching offline variant. Online transitions select kernel versus movable from the zone of the first page while preserving partialness. Fully unplugged blocks are offlined and removed and then marked unused.

Hotplug notifier ignores events outside the device range. Sub-block mode requires whole memory-block granularity and alignment; big-block mode requires the range to stay within one big block, else the event is rejected. Going-offline and going-online acquire the hotplug mutex, refuse while removal is in progress, and mark hotplug active. Offline adds to offline accounting and may requeue work; online subtracts and may requeue when below half threshold and no work is active. Cancel paths restore state and release the mutex.

Fake-offline handling drops one reference per page when going offline and complains if a page was still referenced, then retakes one reference per page if offline is cancelled. Marking fake-offline behaves differently for never-onlined versus onlined pages; clearing reverses it. Fake-online processes the largest feasible aligned power-of-two runs, routing never-onlined pages through the generic online path and allocated ranges through contiguous release plus managed-count adjustment.

Hotplug mutex serializes state-store replacement and the window between going-online or going-offline and its completion or cancellation. Removal uses an interrupt-safe spinlock to test the removing flag before queueing device work, so work is not queued during teardown. Unplugged-block removal temporarily drops the hotplug mutex across the blocking offline-and-remove operation and reacquires it before updating state.

Memory hotplug notifier is the online and offline coordination point for ranges owned by the device, translating the start address to a sub-block or big-block id and dispatching to the matching per-mode helper. Power-management notifier unconditionally vetoes hibernation and restore preparation while accepting other events.

Growth allocation can fail with out-of-memory and leaves the old store intact. Adding memory can fail after accounting, requiring rollback. Offline-plus-remove is expected to succeed because pages were pre-isolated but may still report busy or out-of-memory. Big-block offline helpers act only when the block is in fake-offline state; sub-block going-offline and cancel helpers skip plugged subblocks.
